'''Peeter Saari''' (born 2 June 1945) is an Estonian physicist whose work spans optical spectroscopy of solids, ultrafast optics and wave optics. He was a professor of wave optics at the [[University of Tartu]] (currently a professor ''emeritus'') and has been a member of the [[Estonian Academy of Sciences]] since 1986.<ref name="EAS_member">{{cite web |title=Peeter Saari |website=Estonian Academy of Sciences |url=https://www.akadeemia.ee/en/member/saari/ |access-date=27 January 2026}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Saari was born in [[Tallinn]] on 2 June 1945.<ref name="EAS_member" /> He graduated from Tallinn Secondary School No. 21 in 1963 and received a bachelor's degree in theoretical physics at the [[University of Tartu]] in 1968.<ref name="Tartu_honorary" /><ref name="EAS_75">{{cite web |title=Akadeemik Peeter Saari – 75 |website=Estonian Academy of Sciences |url=https://www.akadeemia.ee/akadeemik-peeter-saari-75/ |access-date=27 January 2026 |language=et}}</ref>

==Career==
Saari's academic career has been closely associated with the Institute of Physics in Tartu, which was formerly part of the Estonian Academy of Sciences and later became part of the University of Tartu.<ref name="EAS_75" /><ref name="Optica_fellow" /> He led the Laboratory of Crystal Spectroscopy (later physical optics) from 1976, and served as director of the institute in 1981–1988.<ref name="EAS_75" /><ref name="EAS_member" />

He defended his Candidate of Sciences dissertation in physics and mathematics in 1972, and his doctoral dissertation in 1980; he was awarded the Doctor of Sciences degree in 1981.<ref name="EAS_75" /><ref name="EAS_member" /> He received the title of professor in 1994 and has been professor of wave optics at the University of Tartu since 1997.<ref name="EAS_member" /><ref name="EAS_75" />

Saari was elected a member of the Estonian Academy of Sciences in 1986 in the field of physics. He belongs to the Department of Mathematics, Astronomy and Physics at the academy and served as the head of the Department of Astronomy and Physics from 2004 to 2009. He was elected a member of the Academia Europaea in 2003 and a Fellow of Optica (the American Optical Society) in 2017.

Since 2021, he has been Professor Emeritus at the University of Tartu.
His CV is available [https://www.etis.ee/CV/Peeter_Saari/eng/ here].

==Research==
Saari's research has included hot luminescence and vibronic relaxation in solids, temporal–spectral diagnostics and synthesis of ultrashort optical pulses, time–space (four-dimensional) holography, and propagation-invariant and other structured light fields in wave optics.<ref name="EAS_75" /><ref name="Optica_fellow" /> In 2000 he received the Estonian National Science Award in exact sciences for a cycle of work on non-diffracting light waves.<ref name="RT_2000_award" />

==Scientific service==
Saari has held scientific leadership roles in Estonia, including service on the governing bodies of the Estonian Academy of Sciences and leadership roles connected with national research funding and science policy.<ref name="EAS_75" /><ref name="Tartu_honorary" />

==Honours and awards==
Among Saari's awards are:
* Estonian National Science Award (exact sciences), 2000<ref name="RT_2000_award" />
* Order of the White Star, III class, 2002<ref name="RT_2002_WhiteStar" />
* J. N. Denisyuk Medal, inventor of spatial holography, from the Rozhdenstvensky Optical Society, 2011 
* Honorary Citizen of Tartu, 2014<ref name="Tartu_honorary" />
* Estonian National Science Award (lifetime achievement), 2019<ref name="RT_2019_award" /><ref name="HM_2019">{{cite web |title=Teaduse elutööpreemia saavad Anne Luik ja Peeter Saari |website=Haridus- ja Teadusministeerium |url=https://www.hm.ee/uudised/teaduse-elutoopreemia-saavad-anne-luik-ja-peeter-saari |access-date=27 January 2026 |language=et}}</ref>
* Optica Fellow, 2017<ref name="Optica_fellow" />
